newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Senate panel approves Banerj loan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Senate panel approves Banerj loan.

text.p: A Brazilian Senate panel approved Tuesday a proposed 3.09 billion-real ($2.89 billion) loan to Rio de Janeiro state which will help pave the way for privatization of state bank Banerj, a Senate official said.
The proposal must now be approved by the floor of the Senate, the official said.

No date has been set for the full Senate vote, the official said. National CBN Radio quoted Rio state planning secretary Marco Aurelio Alencar as saying he was confident the privatization of Banerj would take place Wednesday.
The success of the sale, the first of a Brazilian state bank, hinges on approval of the loan which would be used by Rio to pay off Banerj's pension and payroll-related debts.
The loan would be made by federal mortgage bank Caixa Economica Federal.
Four banks -- Bradesco, Banco Itau, BCN and Cia. de Investimentos Latino-Americana owned by an unidentified foreign bank and represented by local Banco Pactual -- have signed up for the auction.

Banerj was placed under Central Bank control in December 1994 when it failed to meet liquidity requirements and has been prepared for privatization by its managers, investment bank Banco Bozano, Simonsen, since January 1996.
Rio state has set a minimum price of 310 million reais for Banerj, down from an asking price of 480 million reais last year when previous attempts to sell the bank were held up by legal challenges.
